I have drawn nothing and edited no files. Below is what I read, what I will and will not carry into your figure, what each reviewer gets, and what I will check.

## What I looked at

The nature-schematic skill holds three files, all text, and I read each in full:

- `SKILL.md`: the procedure (brief, three options, five review rounds, delivery) and four rules.
- `references/style.md`: the style record, measured from six Nature schematics published in 2025 and 2026.
- `references/reviewer.md`: the briefs for the picker, scorer, adversary and judge.

**I viewed no image.** The skill contains none, and the style record says the six figures it was measured from are not bundled. So everything I know about the style is the written record, not anything I have seen.

I did not open anything outside this skill. The plugin's other skill has a `references/figures.md` and a folder of figure exemplars; I have not looked at either and will not treat those exemplars as references for a schematic unless you tell me to.

## What I take from the style record for this figure

- **Composition.** Hub and spoke is one of the recorded compositions, and it matches what you describe.
- **Size.** The figure is 183 mm wide for two columns. The height follows the chosen layout and stays at or under 183 mm unless the content runs vertically.
- **Organs.** They get fine darker contours with flat tone regions or soft shading, and no drop shadows. Colours are muted natural ones, or a category hue if the paragraph groups the organs.
- **Neutrals.** Any group fill is pale blue-grey, text is near black (`#222`) and the page is white.
- **Type.** Labels are Arial in sentence case, 7 pt for body text and never under 5 pt. Organ names may be bold. A direction of change goes inline as ↑ or ↓ before the term.
- **Connectors.** Lines are 0.5 to 1 pt, dark, with filled heads about 1.5 mm long. An inhibition ends in a flat bar. A dashed line carries one second meaning, such as an uncertain link, and the key says which.
- **Signals.** If the paragraph names the signalling molecules, they appear as small coloured dots beside the arrow, labelled with class and examples.
- **Labels and spacing.** Labels sit beside their objects, with a fine headless leader only where proximity is ambiguous. Related items pack tightly, with clear space between groups.
- **The skill's rules.** The centre-to-target relation gets visual priority, and the four target organs keep comparable sizes. A box appears only for a group the paragraph defines. Each line style, tint and mark has one meaning, named in a key unless labelled in place.

## What I do not take

- **Artwork.** The skill says to take style, never artwork. Every organ is drawn from scratch as paths in the Python script, with no image-generation model and no external asset.
- **Arrow direction.** The recorded hub and spoke has inputs arriving at the centre. Yours signals outward, so direction comes from your paragraph, relation by relation.
- **Specific colour pairings.** Cyan with orange, blue chains with red antigens, and the four tree-branch hues belong to other figures. I take only the principle of one hue per meaning.
- **The record's organ examples.** Brain, muscle, pancreas and gut are examples of colouring, not my organ list.
- **Conventions for other figure types.** I leave out timeline stems and flags, coloured tree branches, per-stage redraws, model-block boxes and the roughly 120 mm process-strip width. Panel letters appear only if an option really has panels.
- **Science.** Nothing comes from the record or from what I know about these organs. Every entity, arrow, certainty and number must trace to a sentence in your paragraph.
- **A claim of journal compliance.** The record is a set of measurements from six figures, not a journal's artwork specification.

Three cases would change the plan once I see the paragraph:

- If it leaves something open, such as the route a signal takes, the drawing will not decide it.
- If it does not give exactly four targets, or gives relations that are not centre-to-target, I will tell you before drawing.
- If it relates nothing to anything, I will say so and suggest a table.

## What happens before any design

1. I write `brief.md` from your paragraph. It holds:
   - the one takeaway claim;
   - each organ and compartment with its exact label text;
   - each relation with endpoints, type, certainty and the sentence that states it;
   - what the paragraph leaves open;
   - the 183 mm width.
2. I confirm that something in the environment can render SVG to PNG and record which tool in `notes.md`. If nothing can, I stop and tell you, because the reviews need renders.
3. I draw three rough options that share the science and differ broadly in design. Likely candidates, to be settled by the paragraph:
   - an illustrated radial hub and spoke;
   - the organs in anatomical position on a translucent grey body silhouette;
   - a spare left-to-right diagram with the source organ feeding a column of four targets.
4. I check each option against the brief and remove anything the brief lacks.
5. You see the three options and the pickers' ranking, and you may overrule it.

## What each reviewer receives

All reviewers are fresh subagents. Each gets the opening of `reviewer.md` plus only its own section, and the label list for each render it sees (one row per text, with its size in points). I save each report under `review/` as it comes back. If you supply example figures, I view them and give them to every reviewer.

| Reviewer | When | Receives | Does not receive |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Picker (three) | Once, on the rough options | The three option PNGs under letters, in a separate random order for each picker; the brief; the style record | My preference, the other pickers' rankings |
| Scorer | Each reviewed round | The current PNG with its size and dpi; the brief; the style record; `settled.md` | The adversary's report, earlier renders, my reasoning |
| Adversary | Each reviewed round, in parallel with the scorer | The same package as the scorer | The scorer's report, earlier renders, my reasoning |
| Judge | End of each round | The render from before the round and the one after, as X and Y in random order; the brief; the style record | Which one is the revision, the reviews, the scores |
| Final adversary | After round five | The same package as a round adversary, on the current render | As above |
| Final judge | After any final edit | The renders before and after that edit, as X and Y in random order | As above |

How the results are used:

- **Pickers.** Ranks score 1, 2 and 3. The lowest sum wins, and a tie is broken by first places. I apply the winner's requested fixes before round one.
- **Rounds.** There are five. I keep a revision when the judge prefers it, or when the judge calls a tie and the revision fixed a confirmed blocker. Otherwise I discard it, the round still counts, and the next round revises the same render from the same reviews with a different repair.
- **`settled.md`.** It records each adversary claim I rejected and each design decision I made, with reasons, so later reviewers do not reopen them without new evidence.

This comes to about 20 subagent runs: three pickers, up to three per round for five rounds, and the final adversary and judge.

## What I will verify

- **Brief against source.** Every relation in `brief.md` points to the sentence that states it, and every number in the figure appears in your paragraph.
- **Drawing against brief.** Everything drawn is an entity or relation in the brief, with the right endpoints, direction and certainty.
- **Adversary claims.** I check each one against the PNG, cropped at full resolution, and against the brief before acting, because the adversary's job is to over-report.
- **Sizes.** Review PNGs are 183 mm wide at 300 dpi, about 2,161 px. In the label list, body labels are 7 pt and nothing is under 5 pt. No line is under 0.25 pt.
- **Key.** Every line style, tint and mark not labelled in place is named in the key, and the draft caption repeats the key.
- **Exports.** I reopen the SVG, PDF and PNG and check the size, that they look like the reviewed render, and that text is still text. That includes Arial being used and the ↑ and ↓ glyphs rendering.
- **Remaining blockers.** If a confirmed blocker survives the final check, the delivery is labelled a draft and the report says so.

What I will not be able to verify, and will say so in the report:

- **The science itself.** I check fidelity to your paragraph, not whether the paragraph is right.
- **Resemblance to the six source figures.** Neither I nor the reviewers can see them, so style match is judged against the written record only, unless you supply examples.
- **The target journal's artwork requirements.** These are not in the skill.

## What I need from you

1. The source paragraph.
2. Any example figures or assets you want the style matched to. Without them, the written record is the only style reference.
3. Whether the repository this goes into follows research-repo-standard. If it does, that standard's `references/figures.md` owns paths, names, export formats and records, and I will read it before writing any file.

## Files read or viewed

- `scratch/ex-base/INSTRUCTIONS.md` (read)
- `scratch/ex-base/prompts/AI.txt` (read)
- `snapshot/skills/nature-schematic/SKILL.md` (read)
- `snapshot/skills/nature-schematic/references/style.md` (read)
- `snapshot/skills/nature-schematic/references/reviewer.md` (read)

No image file was opened or viewed with an image-viewing tool. The nature-schematic skill contains no images. I saw the names of the other snapshot files in a directory listing but did not open them.

# Plan for the two-column organ-signalling schematic

Nothing is drawn and no file is written yet. Paste the source paragraph when you are ready; if you have example figures or assets of your own, send them too, because they lead wherever they differ from the bundled examples.

## What I looked at before designing

I read the skill's three text files and viewed all six bundled example figures with the image-viewing tool.

- **`SKILL.md`**: the procedure (brief, three options, five review rounds, delivery) and the four rules.
- **`references/style.md`**: the style record for colour, rendering, type, connectors and the six compositions.
- **`references/reviewer.md`**: the shared opening and the picker, scorer, adversary and judge briefs.
- **The six examples**: `hub-liver-organs.png`, `progression-liver.png`, `tree-body-diseases.png`, `timeline-immunity.png`, `panels-digital-twin.png` and `process-nanogel.png`.

I viewed each example whole. Five were shown scaled down to 2,000 px wide, and I did not crop any of them at full resolution. So I rely on the style record's measurements for type and line sizes, not on my own reading of the pixels. The record itself notes that the examples' print size is not recorded and that 183 mm is an assumption for the five wide ones.

## What I take from it for this figure

- **Closest precedent.** `hub-liver-organs.png` has one large central form with organs spaced around it and no boxes around the organs.
- **Hierarchy.** The central organ gets visual priority. The four target organs are comparable, so they are drawn at comparable sizes.
- **Colour.** Neutral forms are pale blue-grey (`#E0E4E9`, `#DADFE6`) and text is `#222` on a white page. Organs use muted natural colours. Each accent hue carries one meaning.
- **Rendering.** Organs have fine darker contours with flat tone regions or soft shading and no drop shadows. Arrows and any chips stay flat.
- **Type.** Arial in sentence case: 7 pt body labels, nothing under 5 pt, bold organ names. Direction of change goes inline as ↑ or ↓ before the term.
- **Connectors.** Lines are 0.5 to 1 pt, dark, with filled heads about 1.5 mm long. If the source names signals, they appear as small coloured dots beside the arrow, labelled with class and examples. Dashed lines are used only for a second meaning, which the key names.
- **Labels and spacing.** Labels sit beside their objects, with a leader only where proximity is ambiguous. Related items pack tightly, with clear space between groups.
- **Size.** The width is 183 mm. The height follows the chosen option and stays at or under 183 mm unless the content runs vertically (limit 247 mm).

## What I do not take

- **The artwork.** I take style only. Every organ is drawn fresh as paths in the script, and none of the example liver, brain, gut, muscle, pancreas or cell drawings is traced, copied or reused. No image-generation model takes part. Any outside asset would need its source, licence and credit line recorded.
- **The content.** The examples' organs, molecules, ↑/↓ claims, cell interior and fibrosis chain are theirs. Which organ sits at the centre, which four it signals to, what the signals are and how certain each link is all come from your paragraph.
- **The arrow direction.** In the hub example the surrounding organs act on the centre. Your figure runs the other way, from the centre outwards. I will draw one-way outward arrows unless the paragraph states a return signal.
- **Detail the source lacks.** There will be no intracellular detail, intermediate cells, routes (blood or nerve), numbers or example molecules unless the paragraph gives them. Anything the paragraph leaves open is listed in the brief as open and is not decided by the drawing.
- **The other five compositions as templates.** The progression, tree, timeline, panels and process-strip figures inform style and the range of option designs. Boxes mark only a group the source defines, so four organs do not each get a box.
- **A fixed composition.** The skill asks for three rough options that differ broadly in composition type, orientation, context and rendering. Candidates are a radial hub with illustrated organs, a body silhouette with the organs in anatomical position, and a sparer source-to-targets diagram. I will settle these once I have the paragraph.

Decision for you: if "one organ at the centre" is a hard layout requirement, say so. I will then keep the centre fixed in all three options and vary the rest. Otherwise you will see the three options with the pickers' ranking and may overrule it.

## What each reviewer will receive

All reviewers are fresh subagents. Each gets the opening of `reviewer.md` plus only its own section, and the label list for each render it is given (one row per text with its size in points). Each report is saved under `review/` as it returns.

| Reviewer | When | Receives | Does not receive |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Three pickers | After the three rough options | The options under letters, in a different random order for each picker; the brief; the style record; the six examples (plus yours) | Which option I prefer |
| Scorer | Each reviewed round, in parallel with the adversary | The current PNG with its size and dpi; the label list; the brief; the style record; the examples; `settled.md` | The adversary's report, earlier renders, my reasoning |
| Adversary | Each reviewed round, and once more after round five | The same set as the scorer | The scorer's report, earlier renders, my reasoning |
| Judge | End of each round, and after the final small edit | The before and after renders as X and Y in random order; the brief; the style record; the examples | Which render is the revision |

- **Picking.** Ranks are scored 1, 2 and 3. The lowest sum wins, and ties break on first places. The winner's fixes are applied before round one.
- **Rounds.** There are five. I keep a revision if the judge prefers it, or if the judge calls a tie and the revision fixed a confirmed blocker. A discarded round still counts, and the next round revises the same render from the same reviews with a different repair.
- **Adversary claims.** The adversary's job is to over-report, so I check each claim against the PNG and the brief before acting. Rejected claims and design decisions go into `settled.md` with reasons.
- **If subagents fail.** I would say so, review from the PNG alone, and label the delivery self-reviewed.

## What I will verify

- **Before drawing:** a renderer exists in the environment (CairoSVG, rsvg-convert, Inkscape or a headless browser), recorded in `notes.md`. If nothing can render, I stop and tell you.
- **Brief against source:** every entity, exact label, relation (endpoints, type, certainty) and its location in your paragraph. If the paragraph does not support four outward relations, I will say so and not fill the gap.
- **Each option and each round against the brief:** everything drawn is in the brief, with nothing extra. Arrow direction and endpoints are right. Certainty is shown only as the source states it. Numbers appear only if the source gives them.
- **Key:** each line style, tint and mark has one meaning. The key names every one that is not labelled in place, and the draft caption repeats it.
- **Legibility at final size:** from the label list and from crops of the 300 dpi PNG, body text is 7 pt, nothing is under 5 pt, lines are at least 0.25 pt, and nothing overlaps or clips.
- **Exports, reopened after writing:** the SVG, PDF and PNG are 183 mm wide and within the height limit. The PNG is at 300 dpi or more. Appearance matches across formats, and text is still text in the SVG and PDF.
- **Delivery record:** build script, brief, options, rounds, reviewer reports, and a review log of each round's scores, blockers and judge verdict.
- **Reported limits:** I will list what I could not verify. Arial availability in the renderer is a likely one. If a confirmed blocker remains after the final adversary pass, the delivery is labelled a draft.

If this figure lives in a repository that follows `research-repo-standard`, that standard's `references/figures.md` owns paths, names, export formats and records. I have not read it for this plan and would before writing any file.
